new.descnews: Seafood choices are specific, not universal. Species, stock, origin, fishing gear, farming system, and current health advisories can all change the answer. Use each profile as a starting point, open its sources, and confirm label details before buying.

source.sourcetitle: NOAA Fisheries — Sustainable Seafood for Consumers

new.descnews: FDA/EPA fish categories address mercury for people who are pregnant or breastfeeding and children. They do not grade fisheries or farms. A species can be lower in mercury while still requiring origin-specific sustainability research, or come from a well-managed fishery while carrying mercury advice for sensitive groups.

A market name may cover several species, and one species may be divided into multiple managed stocks. Ask for the scientific or accepted market name, country or region of origin, and whether it was wild-caught or farm-raised.

source.sourcetitle: NOAA Fisheries — Seafood Mislabeling and Fraud

new.descnews: Stock assessments, catch limits, advisories, closures, and production practices change. The app links to the sources behind its summaries so you can see current agency information rather than relying on a frozen rating.
